title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-12-04
lineage: SBD > MC (Owlsley's) > DAT > DAT > CD > EAC > DC5 > CD

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a historic late‑'69 set with a smoking Dark Star and the debut Uncle John’s Band, but tape hiss and a cloudy mix keep it only fair technically.
ai_review.review: The show shines with early‑Dead energy – a blazing 30‑minute Dark Star, a unique Black Peter arrangement, and the first known performance of Uncle John's Band, all highlighted by Tom Constanten's organ on every tune. The soundboard source suffers from tape hiss, a “cloudy” mix and a badly tuned Strat, making the listening experience only moderately clear.

ai_rating.rationale: Average of five reviews (2‑5 stars) gives 3.6; strong musical highlights offset mediocre recording quality, placing the rating in the good‑to‑great range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tape hiss and a generally cloudy mix ('stinky winky'); some reviewers note a badly tuned Strat; organ is prominent but overall clarity is limited.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Late‑'69 set featuring early Workingman's Dead material, organ on every song and a historic first performance of Uncle John's Band; the flow is engaging despite occasional tuning issues.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals were strong and youthful, but his Strat was badly tuned.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten's organ is prominent on every track, adding an early‑Dead texture.
